parts.title: Calorie Counting
parts.summary: Group blank-line-separated positive integer calorie items into per-Elf inventories, compute each Elf's total calories, and find the highest single-Elf calorie total.
parts.algorithmSummary: Single-pass bounded top-k leaderboard scan (k = 1) over immutable ElfInventory value objects (computing totalCalories dynamically from raw items), verified against an independent descending-sort oracle and matching the pre-verified AoC star answer.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Generalizing rankTopElves and traceTopElves to parameter k in 2022/day01/shared/ handles Part 1 (k = 1) and Part 2 (k = 3) with zero parser or engine churn.
Computing totalCalories and itemCount via getters on frozen ElfInventory keeps raw snack items as the single source of truth.

parts.title: Calorie Counting
parts.summary: Using the same blank-line-separated Elf calorie inventories from Part 1, identify the three Elves carrying the highest individual totals and return their combined calorie sum.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2022/day01/shared rankTopElves(inventories, 3) and sumCalories: single-pass bounded top-3 insertion in O(N) time and O(1) extra space, differentially verified against a descending-sort oracle and matching the pre-verified AoC star answer.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) extra tracking space
learnings: Parameterizing the shared leaderboard engine by k let Part 2 achieve 100% coverage in 30 lines of domain code with zero imports from part1/.
Wrapping both parse and trace inside try/catch in the visualizer cleanly handles valid 1- or 2-Elf inputs that reject top-3 selection.

parts.title: Rock Paper Scissors
parts.summary: Score a Rock Paper Scissors strategy guide where A/B/C denote the opponent's Rock/Paper/Scissors and X/Y/Z denote your direct Rock/Paper/Scissors throw, summing shape points (1/2/3) plus outcome points (0/3/6) across all rounds.
parts.algorithmSummary: Cyclic Z_3 modular scoring via shared/core euclideanMod(player - opponent + 1, 3) with immutable StrategyRound, ResolvedRound, and 9-cell MatchupSummary value objects in 2022/day02/shared/; exhaustively tested across all 9 pairs and differentially verified against an explicit 3x3 rule matrix over 2,500 rounds.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) working space
learnings: Using shared/core euclideanMod(player - opponent + 1, 3) avoids JavaScript negative modulo bugs on Scissors vs Rock and mirrors Part 2's inverse formula.
Storing raw A/B/C and X/Y/Z tokens in StrategyRound plus a RoundResolver interface lets Part 2 reinterpret X/Y/Z as desired outcomes with zero parser churn.

parts.title: Rock Paper Scissors
parts.summary: Reinterpret column two (X/Y/Z) as the desired round outcome (Lose/Draw/Win), select the unique player shape achieving that outcome against A/B/C, and sum shape plus outcome points across all rounds.
parts.algorithmSummary: Modular inverse RoundResolver (DesiredOutcomeResolver) plugging into 2022/day02/shared with zero churn: derives playerShape = euclideanMod(opponent + desiredOutcome - 1, 3), verified across all 9 combinations and differentially checked against a hardcoded LUT oracle over 2,500 rounds.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) space
learnings: Inverting the Z_3 outcome equation via shared/core euclideanMod(opponent + desiredOutcome - 1, 3) handles the negative wrap on (Rock, Lose) cleanly and eliminates magic payoff tables.
Reusing MatchupSummary.countOf(opp, derivePlayerShape(opp, outcome)) lets the Part 2 visualizer display the 3x3 target-outcome matrix with zero changes to shared/.

parts.title: Rucksack Reorganization
parts.summary: Split each rucksack string into two equal compartments, find the unique item type present in both halves (a–z = 1–26, A–Z = 27–52), and return the sum of priorities across all rucksacks.
parts.algorithmSummary: 52-bit BigInt bitmask intersection reusing shared/core bigintLog2: immutable Rucksack value objects in 2022/day03/shared/ derive compartment masks dynamically, verify power-of-two uniqueness, and extract 1-based priorities in O(N) time; differentially verified against a Set intersection oracle over 312 rucksacks.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Using 52-bit BigInt bitmasks with shared/core bigintLog2 avoids JavaScript's 32-bit bitwise truncation on uppercase priorities 32..52 and exposes Rucksack.allMask for Part 2 group intersections.
Keeping Rucksack constructor validation structural (even length and ASCII letters) rather than requiring compartment overlap lets Part 2 reuse Rucksack for arbitrary valid lines.

parts.title: Rucksack Reorganization
parts.summary: Partition the ordered rucksacks into consecutive groups of three Elves, identify the unique item type shared by all three Elves in each group (ignoring compartments), and return the sum of badge priorities.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2022/day03/shared Rucksack.allMask and extractSinglePriority via immutable ElfGroup value objects intersecting a.allMask & b.allMask & c.allMask in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space; differentially verified against a 3-way Set intersection oracle over 156 groups.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Exposing Rucksack.allMask in 2022/day03/shared let Part 2 compute 3-Elf group badges with a single 3-way BigInt bitwise AND and zero edits to shared/ or part1/.
Passing three explicit Rucksack arguments to ElfGroup's constructor guarantees valid group arity at compile time without dead runtime length branches.

parts.title: Camp Cleanup
parts.summary: Parse pairs of inclusive integer section assignment ranges (a-b,c-d) and count how many pairs have one range completely containing the other.
parts.algorithmSummary: Direct closed-interval endpoint containment scan over immutable AssignmentPair value objects built on shared/core ClosedInterval in 2022/day04/shared/, classifying all 5 PairRelation states dynamically and differentially verified against both sign-product and bitset-subset oracles over 1,000 synthetic pairs.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Avoid IntervalUnion for pair overlap/containment checks because it coalesces integer-adjacent ranges like [2,3] and [4,5].
Scaling SVG interval bars by totalUnits = bounds.end - bounds.start + 1n in BigInt prevents divide-by-zero on single-point domains and keeps huge ranges exact.

parts.title: Camp Cleanup
parts.summary: Using the same pairs of inclusive integer section assignment ranges (a-b,c-d), count how many pairs overlap at all (sharing at least one section ID).
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn closed-interval overlap scan reusing 2022/day04/shared AssignmentPair.overlaps and PairRelation classification in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space; differentially verified against both an endpoint-sweep oracle and a bitset-intersection oracle across 1,000 synthetic pairs.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Reusing AssignmentPair.overlaps and 5-way PairRelation from 2022/day04/shared delivered Part 2 with zero edits to shared/ and zero imports from part1/.

Drawing single-point endpoint touches as a distinct diamond marker and only showing a gap bracket when upper.start > lower.end + 1n visually separates overlapping, adjacent-disjoint, and gapped-disjoint ranges.

parts.title: Supply Stacks
parts.summary: Parse an ASCII drawing of numbered crate stacks and a sequence of move commands, simulate CrateMover 9000 lifting crates one at a time (reversing lifted order), and read the top crate label from every stack.
parts.algorithmSummary: Encapsulated in-place stack simulation parameterized by a CraneStrategy interface (CrateMover9000 LIFO reversal) in 2022/day05/shared/ with whitespace-preserving diagram parsing and gravity validation in O(C + K) time; differentially verified against an independent O(S * M) reverse top-crate coordinate tracker across 45 seeded random procedures.
parts.complexity: O(C + K) time, O(S + C) space
learnings: Never .trim() raw input or diagram lines when parsing ASCII crate drawings; leading spaces encode empty left columns while stripped trailing spaces on short lines must still be tolerated.

Parameterizing executeProcedure and traceProcedure by CraneStrategy and placing the pure React Cargo Crane Bay SVG in 2022/day05/shared/viz/ makes Part 2 (CrateMover 9001) zero-churn across both domain and UI.

parts.title: Supply Stacks
parts.summary: Execute the same crate rearrangement procedure with the CrateMover 9001, which lifts count crates as a single contiguous block preserving their vertical order, and read the top crate label from every stack.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn CrateMover9001 CraneStrategy plugging into 2022/day05/shared executeProcedure, traceProcedure, and CraneBayVisualizer: shallow-clones and freezes the lifted bottom-to-top slice intact in O(N + sum(count)) time; differentially verified against an order-preserving O(S * M) backward top-tracker oracle across 50 seeded random procedures.
parts.complexity: O(N + sum(count)) time, O(N) space
learnings: Because 2022/day05/shared separated CraneStrategy and placed CraneBayVisualizer in shared/viz/, Part 2 required only 41 lines of domain code and a 15-line visualizer wrapper with zero edits to shared/.
Defensive shallow cloning and freezing inside CrateMover9001.arrangeLifted prevents aliasing bugs when direct unit-test callers mutate their source array.

parts.title: Tuning Trouble
parts.summary: Scan a single-line lowercase ASCII datastream buffer to find the 1-based end position of the first contiguous 4-character start-of-packet marker whose characters are all pairwise distinct.
parts.algorithmSummary: Monotonic last-seen jump window parameterized by windowSize in 2022/day06/shared/ using a 26-entry Int32Array (-1 sentinel) in O(N) time and O(1) space independent of window width, paired with a reusable SignalTapeVisualizer in 2022/day06/shared/viz/ for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against both a Set window oracle and a 26-bit XOR parity oracle (reusing shared/core bitCount) across 60+ PRNG strings.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) space
learnings: Guarding prev >= start in the last-seen jump window prevents stale pre-window duplicates from pulling the left boundary backward while running in O(N) independent of windowSize K.
Parameterizing createMarkerSolver(windowSize) and SignalTapeVisualizer in 2022/day06/shared/ prepares Part 2 (windowSize = 14) with zero shared-module churn.

parts.title: Tuning Trouble
parts.summary: Scan the same lowercase ASCII datastream buffer to find the 1-based end position of the first contiguous 14-character start-of-message marker whose characters are all pairwise distinct.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2022/day06/shared createMarkerSolver(14) and SignalTapeVisualizer: monotonic last-seen jump window over a 26-entry Int32Array in O(N) time and O(1) space; differentially verified against both a Set window oracle and a BigInt XOR parity oracle (reusing shared/core bitCount) across 40 seeded streams.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) space
learnings: Parameterizing createMarkerSolver(windowSize) and SignalTapeVisualizer in 2022/day06/shared/ reduced Part 2 to 6 lines of domain code and a 14-line visualizer wrapper with zero edits to shared/.
Using BigInt masks in the test-only XOR parity oracle (mask ^= 1n << BigInt(code)) plugs directly into shared/core bitCount without 32-bit sign-bit edge cases.

parts.title: No Space Left On Device
parts.summary: Replay a terminal navigation and directory listing transcript to reconstruct the filesystem tree rooted at '/', compute each directory's recursive total size, and sum all directories with total size at most 100,000.
parts.algorithmSummary: Immutable FilesystemTree built from an encapsulated canonical-path builder in 2022/day07/shared/ with single-pass O(D + F) post-order DFS metrics and a reusable log-scaled DirectoryAuditSvg in 2022/day07/shared/viz/ for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against a path-stack prefix accumulator oracle across 30 seeded random terminal logs up to ~200 directories and depth 9.
parts.complexity: O(L) time, O(D + F) space
learnings: Personal inputs reuse identical directory basenames across unrelated subtrees and even across nested parent/child directories (/a/a), so directories must always be keyed by canonical path or tree-node identity rather than basename.
Log-scaling directory sizes (log10(bytes + 1)) in the shared stacked bar chart keeps 584-byte subdirectories, the 100,000-byte threshold line, and a 48 MB root simultaneously legible.

parts.title: No Space Left On Device
parts.summary: Given a 70,000,000-byte disk requiring at least 30,000,000 bytes of free space, find the smallest single directory whose deletion frees enough space to run the update and return its total size.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn post-order threshold scan reusing 2022/day07/shared FilesystemTree, DirectoryMetrics, and DirectoryAuditSvg: computes minRequiredToDelete = max(0, 30_000_000 - (70_000_000 - rootTotalSize)) and selects the minimum qualifying directory in O(D) time and O(D) space; differentially verified against a path-stack prefix accumulator oracle across seeded random terminal logs.
parts.complexity: O(L) time, O(D + F) space
learnings: Reusing FilesystemTree, DirectoryMetrics, and the log-scaled DirectoryAuditSvg in 2022/day07/shared/ delivered Part 2 with zero edits to shared/ and zero imports from part1/.
Handling the already-sufficient-free-space boundary (minRequiredToDelete = 0) and exact-threshold equality (>= rather than >) prevents subtle off-by-one bugs.

parts.title: Treetop Tree House
parts.summary: Given a rectangular 2D grid of single-digit tree heights (0–9), count how many trees are visible from outside the grid along any of the four cardinal lines of sight (all intervening trees strictly shorter).
parts.algorithmSummary: 4-pass strictly-decreasing monotonic stack sightlines engine in 2022/day08/shared/ built on shared/core Grid2D and DIRS_4 with a reusable 10-slot Int32Array stack in O(R * C) time (2.72 ms on 99x99): computes both explicit 4-bit visibilityMask and all 4 Int32Array viewing distances in one pass, paired with a 10-band batched-SVG CanopySightlineSvg visualizer for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified cell-by-cell against a direct DIRS_4 ray-cast oracle across 30 seeded rectangular grids.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Replacing equal-height entries on the monotonic stack (after recording viewing distance) bounds stack depth to <= 10 across heights 0..9 while tracking visibility explicitly via 4-bit masks to avoid edge-blocker false positives.

Batching 9,801 grid cells into 10 elevation-band SVG <path> elements in 2022/day08/shared/viz/CanopySightlineSvg.tsx keeps 99x99 interactive ray inspection crisp at ~30 SVG DOM nodes and ready for zero-churn Part 2 scenic mode.

parts.title: Treetop Tree House
parts.summary: Compute every tree's scenic score as the product of its four cardinal viewing distances (counting trees up to and including the first tree of equal or greater height, or the grid edge), and return the highest scenic score in the forest.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn monotonic-stack scenic scan reusing 2022/day08/shared ForestGrid, ForestSightlines, and CanopySightlineSvg (mode='scenic'): precomputes all four directional viewing distances in O(R * C) time (3.88 ms on 99x99) and scans interior rows with deterministic row-major tie-breaking via ScenicScanTimeline and ScenicTraceFrame (zero stored derived state); differentially verified against an independent DIRS_4 direct-ray oracle across 60 seeded rectangular grids and 99x99 scale.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Precomputing all four viewing distances inside 2022/day08/shared/ForestSightlines and wiring CanopySightlineSvg mode='scenic' delivered Part 2 with zero edits to shared/ and zero imports from part1/.
Evaluating sightlines.scenicScore(row, col) before checking row <= scannedRow inside isInteriorScanned ensures out-of-bounds coordinates always throw RangeError rather than silently returning false.

parts.title: Rope Bridge
parts.summary: Simulate a 2-knot rope (head and tail) starting at (0, 0) under cardinal head motion commands where the tail pulls one orthogonal or diagonal step whenever Chebyshev distance exceeds 1, and count distinct cells visited by the tail.
parts.algorithmSummary: Generalized K-knot Int32Array rope stepper (K = 2) with early-break cascade and polymorphic DenseTailTracker (Uint8Array) / SparseTailTracker (Set<string>) in 2022/day09/shared/ (2.27 ms across ~11,500 head steps), paired with a pure-TS RopeViewport and HiDPI Canvas 2D RopeBridgeVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 (K = 10) reuse; differentially verified against an independent point-object + Set<string> oracle across 50 seeded PRNG motion plans and multi-knot diagonal cascades.
parts.complexity: O(M + S * K) time, O(K + min(W * H, V)) space
learnings: Using the unified 16-case Math.sign Chebyshev pull rule and parameterizing knotCount in 2022/day09/shared/ handles both Part 1 (K = 2) and Part 2's (±2, ±2) diagonal cascades (K = 10) with zero shared-module churn.
Keeping knot coordinates in world space and applying (-minX, -minY) shifting solely inside DenseTailTracker avoids shift/unshift boilerplate while bounding dense grid memory to <= 4 MB.

parts.title: Rope Bridge
parts.summary: Extend the rope simulation to 10 knots (head plus 9 trailing knots) starting at (0, 0) under the same cardinal head motions—including (±2, ±2) diagonal cascades—and count distinct cells visited by the 10th knot.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn 10-knot specialization (PART2_KNOT_COUNT = 10) reusing 2022/day09/shared Int32Array rope cascade, adaptive DenseTailTracker/SparseTailTracker, and HiDPI Canvas 2D RopeBridgeVisualizer with zero edits to shared/ (2.85 ms across ~11,500 head steps); differentially verified against an independent explicit 4-branch follow oracle covering all 4 (±2, ±2) diagonal quadrants, sparse fallback, and 45 seeded Mulberry32 PRNG plans.
parts.complexity: O(M + S * K) time, O(K + min(W * H, V)) space
learnings: Parameterizing knotCount and implementing the unified Math.sign Chebyshev follow rule in 2022/day09/shared/ reduced Part 2 to 15 lines of production domain code and an 8-line visualizer wrapper with zero shared-module churn.

Asserting that all four (±2, ±2) diagonal cascade quadrants actually fire inside the differential oracle proves Part 2's diagonal pull physics is thoroughly exercised beyond Part 1's orthogonal-head subset.

parts.title: Cathode-Ray Tube
parts.summary: Execute a sequence of 1-cycle noop and 2-cycle addx V CPU instructions updating register X (starting at 1) after each instruction finishes, and sum the signal strengths (cycle * X) sampled during cycles 20, 60, 100, 140, 180, and 220.
parts.algorithmSummary: Direct cycle-level Int32Array RegisterTimeline in 2022/day10/shared/ mapping every 1-based cycle directly to its during-cycle X value in O(N + C) time (0.44 ms across 240 cycles), paired with a reusable SVG OscilloscopeChart and CrtTimelineVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 CRT raster reuse; differentially verified against an event-driven instruction clock oracle across official examples and 40 seeded random programs.
parts.complexity: O(N + C) time, O(C) space
learnings: Storing every during-cycle register X value in an encapsulated Int32Array RegisterTimeline (indexed by 1-based cycle) makes both Part 1 signal sampling and Part 2's 240-cycle 40x6 CRT beam scan O(1) per cycle with zero shared-module churn.
Splitting addx V into two explicit execution cycles while updating X only after the second cycle completes eliminates off-by-one timing bugs at sample boundaries.

parts.title: Cathode-Ray Tube
parts.summary: Drive a 40x6 CRT beam at 1 pixel per cycle using register X as the center of a 3-pixel horizontal sprite ([X-1, X, X+1]), render the 240-cycle bitmap, and decode the eight capital letters displayed on screen.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn 40x6 CRT rasterizer and 30-bit 5x6 bitmap OCR decoder reusing 2022/day10/shared CpuProgram and CpuTimeline in O(C) time (0.54 ms across 240 cycles): stores only a private 240-byte Uint8Array inside immutable CrtScreen, packs 5x6 glyph masks dynamically into a collision-checked 19-template AoC font map, and renders an interactive phosphor CRT monitor with live 3px sprite bracket and progressive 8-slot OCR ribbon; verified against an independent streaming string-OCR oracle and constructive 2-pixel-pair round-trip encoder covering every font glyph.
parts.complexity: O(N + C) time, O(C) space
learnings: Packing each 5x6 CRT slot into a 30-bit integer mask checks the separator column strictly (rejecting stray noise) while supporting 5-wide glyphs like Y with zero sign-bit overflow and O(1) Map lookup.

Because X starts at 1 and cannot change before end of cycle 2, pixels (0,0) and (0,1) are always lit ('##'); a constructive 2-pixel-pair encoder verifies every single glyph in the font table end-to-end through CpuProgram -> CpuTimeline -> CrtScreen -> OCR.

parts.title: Monkey in the Middle
parts.summary: Simulate 20 rounds of monkey keep-away where each monkey inspects every item in its FIFO queue, transforms its worry level, applies floor(worry / 3) relief, and throws it by divisibility test; return monkey business (the product of the top two inspection counts).
parts.algorithmSummary: Queue-free per-item independent trajectory simulation in exact BigInt (O(M) working space, 1.08 ms across 20 rounds) parameterized by polymorphic WorryOperation and KeepAwayRule (DivideByThreeRule using shared/core floorDiv) with dynamic KeepAwaySetup.commonModulus via shared/core lcmBigInt in 2022/day11/shared/, paired with a circular ThrowNetworkSvg and KeepAwayVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 (10,000-round mod-LCM) reuse; differentially verified against an independent round-by-round FIFO queue oracle across official snapshots, 10,000-round modular relief, and 80 seeded random setups.
parts.complexity: O(R * I * H) time, O(M) working space
learnings: Because items never interact and each monkey drains its entire queue every turn, simulating each item independently with round += 1 iff nextMonkey < currentMonkey eliminates queue allocations while matching FIFO order exactly.

Computing KeepAwaySetup.commonModulus dynamically via shared/core lcmBigInt and parameterizing KeepAwayRule.relieve(worry, commonModulus) prepares Part 2 (10,000 rounds mod LCM) with zero shared-module edits.

parts.title: Monkey in the Middle
parts.summary: Run the same monkey keep-away game for 10,000 rounds without divide-by-3 worry relief, preserving exact divisibility routing via modular reduction modulo the LCM of all monkey divisors, and return the product of the top two inspection counts.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn ModularReliefRule (10,000 rounds, worry % commonModulus) plugging into 2022/day11/shared queue-free per-item trajectory simulation and KeepAwayVisualizer with zero shared edits (13.92 ms in exact BigInt across 10,000 rounds / 36 items); differentially verified against both a no-LCM CRT per-divisor residue-vector oracle (prod Z/d_k Z) across composite/shared-factor divisor graphs and a synchronous FIFO queue oracle.
parts.complexity: O(R * I * H) time, O(M) working space
learnings: Because every monkey operation is a polynomial over non-negative integers, reducing worry modulo lcm(d_0, ..., d_{M-1}) is a ring homomorphism preserving every divisibility test identically across 10,000 rounds while running in 13.92 ms in exact BigInt.
Cross-checking against a no-LCM CRT per-divisor residue-vector oracle (tracking w mod d_k independently for each monkey) proves the modular homomorphism sound even on non-coprime composite divisors.

parts.title: Hill Climbing Algorithm
parts.summary: Find the shortest 4-directional path from start S (elevation 'a') to summit E (elevation 'z') on a 2D lowercase heightmap where each step climbs at most +1 elevation (dropping any amount is allowed).
parts.algorithmSummary: Single-pass reverse BFS from E using flat Int32Array queue/distance/parent buffers (neighborHeight >= currentHeight - 1) parameterized by polymorphic StartCondition (FIXED_START_CONDITION) in 2022/day12/shared/ in O(R * C) time (4.21 ms on 41x181), exposing nullable distanceAt/nextStepFrom APIs and pairing with a HiDPI ElevationCanvas and HillClimbingVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 ('a'-elevation start) reuse; differentially verified against an independent forward-BFS oracle in both single-start and multi-source 'a' modes across 60 seeded random heightmaps.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Running reverse BFS from summit E along reversed climb edges (neighborHeight >= currHeight - 1) produces a distance-sorted visitOrder that unifies Part 1 (S) and Part 2 (nearest 'a') via a 5-line StartCondition predicate with zero shared-module edits.

Keeping -1 strictly internal to private Int32Arrays and returning number | null at the ReverseBfsField public boundary makes the classic dist <= frame.distance unreachable-cell bug impossible in TypeScript.

parts.title: Hill Climbing Algorithm
parts.summary: Find the shortest 4-directional path to summit E (elevation 'z') starting from any square at elevation 'a' (including S), where each step may climb at most +1 elevation.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn LOWEST_ELEVATION_START_CONDITION (elevation === 0) plugging into 2022/day12/shared reverse BFS from E and HiDPI ElevationCanvas/HillClimbingVisualizer with zero shared edits in O(R * C) time (4.20 ms on 41x181): selects the first reachable 'a'-elevation square in reverse-BFS distance order; differentially verified against an independent multi-source forward BFS oracle across official examples, unreachable-S fallback, and 60 seeded random heightmaps.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Parameterizing StartCondition on ReverseBfsField in 2022/day12/shared/ reduced Part 2 to a 7-line predicate (LOWEST_ELEVATION_START_CONDITION) and a 5-line solver wrapper with zero edits to shared/ or part1/.
Reverse BFS from summit E naturally handles heightmaps where S itself is cut off from E while another 'a'-elevation trailhead reaches the summit.

parts.title: Distress Signal
parts.summary: Parse pairs of recursively nested integer/list distress-signal packets, determine which pairs are in strictly right order under the recursive int/list/mixed-promotion comparison rules, and sum their 1-based pair indices.
parts.algorithmSummary: Strict recursive-descent AST parser (PacketInt/PacketList/SignalInput, MAX_PACKET_DEPTH = 128) and zero-allocation recursive comparator (comparePackets via compareLists/compareIntToList/negateOrder) in 2022/day13/shared/ in O(N) time (2.74 ms across 150 pairs), paired with a decoupled step-by-step PacketComparePanel and PairIndexGrid visualizer for zero-churn Part 2 divider-packet sorting reuse; differentially verified against an independent JSON.parse + literal [n]-wrapping oracle across official examples, empty-list towers, multi-digit integers, and 150 seeded random packet trees validating reflexivity, skew-symmetry, and transitivity.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Implementing compareIntToList directly without allocating temporary [n] arrays keeps packet comparison zero-allocation on the hot path, while traceComparison wraps mixed ints into PacketList([int]) so traceComparison(l, r).outcome === comparePackets(l, r) acts as an independent structural cross-check.

Day 13 packet comparison is a total preorder (strict weak ordering) rather than strictly antisymmetric on tree identity ([4] === [[4]]), so algebraic property tests should assert reflexivity, skew-symmetry (no -0), and transitivity.

parts.title: Distress Signal
parts.summary: Ignore blank lines, insert divider packets [[2]] and [[6]], order all packets by the recursive Distress Signal comparison rules, and multiply the 1-based sorted indices of the two divider packets to obtain the decoder key.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn single-pass O(N) 3-band divider-rank partitioning reusing 2022/day13/shared SignalInput.packets, parsePacket, comparePackets, traceComparison, and PacketComparePanel with zero shared edits (2.52 ms across 300 packets): short-circuits packets < [[2]] by transitivity ([[2]] < [[6]]) and computes (1 + beforeFirst) * (2 + beforeFirst + between), matching prepended stable sort identically even on equivalent divider ties; differentially verified against an independent JSON.parse + literal [n]-wrapping full stable sort oracle across official examples (140), divider tie/near-tie suites, and 120 seeded random corpora.
parts.complexity: O(N * L) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Partitioning packets into three bands (< [[2]], [[2]]..[[6]], > [[6]]) computes the exact decoder key in O(N) without sorting non-divider packets, while matching ES2019+ prepended stable sort identically even when input packets tie a divider.
Decoupling PacketComparePanel from PacketPair in 2022/day13/shared/viz/ enabled Part 2 to inspect deciding divider comparisons with zero edits to shared/ and zero imports from part1/.

parts.title: Regolith Reservoir
parts.summary: Simulate sand pouring one grain at a time from (500, 0) into a 2D cave of axis-aligned rock polylines (falling down, down-left, then down-right) and count how many units come to rest before sand begins falling into the endless abyss.
parts.algorithmSummary: Stack-resumed DFS over a single encapsulated Int32Array (-1 rock, 0 air, 1..N grain settlement order) parameterized by polymorphic CaveBoundaryPolicy (ABYSS_BOUNDARY_POLICY with tight cone-clamped bounds) in 2022/day14/shared/ in O(W * H) time (2.19 ms across 149 rock paths / 793 grains): captures the exact abyss escape stream directly from the residual stack and pairs with a HiDPI Canvas 2D ReservoirCanvas/ReservoirVisualizer (with floor-band rendering built in) for zero-churn Part 2 floor reuse; differentially verified on both count and exact settled coordinate sets against an independent grain-by-grain Set<string> oracle across official examples (24), blocked source, out-of-cone rocks, negative-x walls, and 50 seeded random caves.
parts.complexity: O(W * H) time, O(W * H) space
learnings: Because cave occupancy grows monotonically, resuming each sand grain from the previous grain's descent stack visits every reachable cell at most once in O(W * H) while preserving exact physical settlement order and yielding the Part 1 abyss escape path for free.
Storing 1..N grain order directly inside one private Int32Array powers zero-copy timeline scrubbing across 160 frames while keeping CaveBoundaryPolicy open for zero-churn Part 2 floor injection.

parts.title: Regolith Reservoir
parts.summary: Replace the endless abyss with an infinite horizontal bedrock floor at y = maxY + 2 and count how many units of sand settle before a grain finally blocks the source at (500, 0).
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn FLOOR_BOUNDARY_POLICY (floorY = scan.maxY + 2, cone bounds [500 - floorY, 500 + floorY], isEscape = () => false) plugging into 2022/day14/shared stack-resumed Int32Array DFS and ReservoirVisualizer/ReservoirCanvas with zero shared edits (3.20 ms across 52k cone cells / 24,166 settled grains): fills row floorY with CELL_ROCK during rasterization so every stack step stays strictly in-bounds; differentially verified on both exact settled grain count and exact (x, y) coordinate sets against an independent row-by-row top-down reachability DP oracle across official examples (93), under-roof hollow pockets, blocked source, out-of-cone rocks, and 50 seeded random caves.
parts.complexity: O(H^2) time, O(H^2) space
learnings: Injecting an 11-line FLOOR_BOUNDARY_POLICY into 2022/day14/shared delivered Part 2 (24,166 grains in 3.20 ms) with zero edits to shared/ or part1/, while preserving chronological pouring animation and bedrock floor rendering.

Cross-checking stack-resumed sand DFS against top-down row reachability DP (sand(x,y) = !rock(x,y) && any parent reachable) proves exact settled-cell set equality including triangular hollow pockets beneath horizontal ceilings.

parts.title: Beacon Exclusion Zone
parts.summary: From sensor-to-nearest-beacon Manhattan distance reports, count how many integer positions on row y = 2,000,000 cannot contain an unknown beacon (union of sensor row slices minus distinct known beacons on that row).
parts.algorithmSummary: Exact BigInt Manhattan row-slice projection coalesced via shared/core ClosedInterval and IntervalUnion in 2022/day15/shared/ in O(S log S) time (0.40 ms across 28 sensors): encapsulates SensorReading with dynamic BigInt radius, covers, rowSlice, and outerDiagonals (preparing zero-churn Part 2 O(S^2) perimeter-line intersection) and pairs with an isotropic projected SensorMapSvg visualizer with optional Part 2 overlays; differentially verified against an independent point-by-point brute-force coverage scanner across all official example rows y in [-2..22] (y = 10 -> 26), shared beacons, tangent slices, and 60 seeded random layouts.
parts.complexity: O(S log S) time, O(S) space
learnings: Every known beacon on row y is necessarily an endpoint of its reporting sensor's Manhattan slice, so excluded(y) equals mergedCoverage.totalLength minus distinctBeaconXsOnRow(readings, y).size with zero redundant containment checks.

Computing radius, rowSlice, covers, and outerDiagonals in exact BigInt inside 2022/day15/shared/sensorReading.ts eliminates safe-integer overflow while preparing Part 2's O(S^2) diagonal intersection with zero shared-module churn.

parts.title: Beacon Exclusion Zone
parts.summary: Find the unique integer point inside [0, 4,000,000]^2 not covered by any sensor's Manhattan exclusion diamond and return its tuning frequency (x * 4,000,000 + y).
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn mathematically complete O(S^3) outer-diagonal intersection search reusing 2022/day15/shared SensorReading.outerDiagonals, covers(), and SensorMapSvg with zero shared edits (12.37 ms across 28 sensors, exact BigInt tuning frequency): enumerates all 4 search-box corners, diagonal-to-box-edge intersections, even (s + d) diagonal intersections, and all 4 surrounding lattice corners for odd (s + d) diagonal diamond-pinches via exact floor division k = (s + d - 1n) / 2n, enforcing strict uniqueness and bounding revealed SVG candidates to maxSteps; differentially verified against an independent row-by-row mergedRowCoverage interval-gap oracle across official examples (56000011), corners, edges, odd-parity pinches, and 40 seeded random [0, 25]^2 layouts.
parts.complexity: O(S^3) time, O(S^2) space
learnings: Adding search-box corners, box-edge intersections, and the 4 lattice points around odd (s + d) intersections via exact floor k = (s + d - 1n) / 2n makes outer-diagonal candidate search 100% mathematically complete—including diagonal diamond-pinch interiors that naive even-parity intersection misses.
Pre-building SensorReading.outerDiagonals and optional Part 2 overlays on SensorMapSvg enabled Part 2 to ship with zero edits to 2022/day15/shared/ and zero imports from part1/.

parts.title: Proboscidea Volcanium
parts.summary: Navigate a network of tunnels starting at valve AA with a 30-minute limit (1 minute to move along a tunnel, 1 minute to open a valve) and maximize total cumulative pressure released by opened valves.
parts.algorithmSummary: BFS graph compression onto K = 15 reachable positive-flow valves sorted by descending flowRate + admissible Rearrangement-Inequality Branch-and-Bound DFS (findOptimalSchedule) and exact feasibility-pruned per-mask Int32Array DP (computeBestByMask) in 2022/day16/shared/ (2.37 ms on 60 valves / 15 positive valves): validates allowedMask non-wrapping bounds, guards directed-tunnel unreachability and overflow, exposes MaskPressureTable.copyScores() + multi-agent buildValveTimeline/ValveNetworkSvg for zero-churn Part 2 SOS Max-DP reuse; differentially verified against an independent uncompressed minute-by-minute raw-network DP oracle across official examples (1651 at T=30 and 1707 at T=26 via SOS DP), positive-flow AA, directed edges, and 35 seeded random valve networks.
parts.complexity: O(K * (V + E)) compression + Branch-and-Bound DFS (< 3 ms), O(2^K) mask table
learnings: Separating admissible Branch-and-Bound (findOptimalSchedule for single-agent optimal routes) from feasibility-pruned MaskPressureTable (computeBestByMask with no global-best pruning) solves Part 1 in 2.37 ms while preparing Part 2's O(K * 2^K) SOS Max-DP with zero edits to 2022/day16/shared/.
Checking (remainingMask & (1 << node)) !== 0 for the first opening slot tightens the Rearrangement-Inequality upper bound even when AA has positive flowRate and is excluded from allowedMask.

parts.title: Proboscidea Volcanium
parts.summary: After spending 4 minutes teaching an elephant to help (leaving 26 minutes), simultaneously coordinate two agents starting at valve AA opening disjoint subsets of positive-flow valves to maximize combined cumulative pressure released.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn block-strided O(K * 2^K) Sum-over-Subsets (SOS) Max-DP with exact argmax submask tracking reusing 2022/day16/shared computeBestByMask, findOptimalSchedule, buildValveTimeline, and ValveNetworkSvg with zero shared edits (8.33 ms on K = 15 positive valves / 32,768 masks): validates DualAgentPlan masks against MAX_INT32 with dynamic totalPressure and openedMask getters, canonicalizes humanScore >= elephantScore, and reconstructs both disjoint agent routes on demand for 2-agent SVG animation; differentially verified against both an independent O(3^K) submask-enumeration oracle and a direct raw-ValveNetwork minute-by-minute 2-agent joint DP oracle across official example (1707), K = 0/1, positive-flow AA, and hub/wing topologies.
parts.complexity: O(T_dfs(K, 26) + K * 2^K) time, O(2^K) space
learnings: Block-strided Sum-over-Subsets Max-DP over MaskPressureTable reduces disjoint two-agent partition search from O(3^K) to O(K * 2^(K-1)) while recovering exact disjoint argmax masks so findOptimalSchedule reconstructs both routes in < 2 ms with zero shared-module edits.

Bounding DualAgentPlan masks to [0, MAX_INT32] before bitwise & / | prevents silent 32-bit JS wrapping on invalid synthetic masks, and computing totalPressure/openedMask via getters maintains a single source of truth.

parts.title: Pyroclastic Flow
parts.summary: Simulate 2,022 non-rotating polyomino rocks (cycling through 5 shapes) falling into a 7-unit-wide vertical chamber under a repeating left/right hot-gas jet stream and return the resulting tower height.
parts.algorithmSummary: Packed 32-bit rock/window bitwise chamber physics + exact top-down {down, left, right} reachable-cavity bisimulation cycle fast-forwarding in BigInt in 2022/day17/shared/ (3.45 ms for 2,022 rocks): packs each 4-row rock into a bit-31-safe 32-bit int with O(1) wall/collision shifts, encapsulates a floor-sentinel row array (rows[0] = 0x7F) with dynamic height and zero stored derived state, and exposes BigInt simulateTower/traceTower plus HiDPI ChamberCanvas/PyroclasticVisualizer (rendering reachable cavity tint and BigInt height ruler) for zero-churn Part 2 (10^12 rocks) reuse; differentially verified against an independent 2D Set<string> coordinate simulator across rocks 1..2,022 on the official example (3068), Part 2 lookahead (1,514,285,714,288), overhang/pocket patterns, and seeded random jet streams.
parts.complexity: O(min(N, S + P) * (F + D)) time, O(min(N, S + P) * D) space
learnings: Because falling rocks only move down, left, or right, a single top-down horizontal-flood reachability sweep from y = height down to 1 computes the exact reachable empty cavity R(C), making (rockIdx, jetIdx, R(C)) a mathematically sound bisimulation invariant for cycle fast-forwarding even under arbitrary overhangs.

Packing 4 chamber rows of 7-bit masks (bit 7 always 0) into a non-negative 32-bit int turns every jet push and downward fall collision check into two bitwise operations while keeping Part 2's 10^12-rock solver zero-churn.

parts.title: Pyroclastic Flow
parts.summary: Determine the exact tower height in the 7-unit-wide falling-rock chamber after 1,000,000,000,000 (10^12) rocks have come to rest under the repeating jet stream.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn PART2_ROCK_COUNT = 1_000_000_000_000n specialization reusing 2022/day17/shared exact top-down reachable-cavity bisimulation cycle fast-forwarding in BigInt and PyroclasticVisualizer/ChamberCanvas with zero shared edits (3.59 ms on ~10k-jet personal input): detects the exact repeating (rockIdx, jetIdx, reachableProfile) state, skips floor((10^12 - dropped) / cycleLength) cycles in exact BigInt arithmetic, and simulates the remaining drops directly; differentially verified against an independent 2D boolean-grid simulator + 2D BFS cavity cycle finder + un-accelerated linearity checks (height(prefix + k * period + rem) === height(prefix + rem) + k * cycleHeight for k = 1..3) across the official example (1,514,285,714,288), sealing periodic streams, and seeded prime-length PRNG streams.
parts.complexity: O((mu + lambda) * (F + D)) time, O((mu + lambda) * D) space
learnings: Pre-building BigInt reachable-cavity cycle skipping and 13-digit BigInt height rulers in 2022/day17/shared/ delivered Part 2 (10^12 rocks in 3.59 ms) with 22 lines of production domain code and zero shared-module edits.

Degenerate non-sealing jet streams (such as pure '<') leave at least one column open to the floor forever, so oracle tests for top-down cavity bisimulation should pair sealing periodic and prime-length PRNG streams with un-accelerated multi-period linearity checks.

parts.title: Boiling Boulders
parts.summary: Given 3D integer coordinates of 1x1x1 lava droplet voxels, compute the total surface area by counting all orthogonal voxel faces not immediately adjacent to another lava cube.
parts.algorithmSummary: 1-cell padded dense 3D Uint8Array VoxelDroplet + flat Int32Array ExteriorFlood BFS in 2022/day18/shared/ in O(N + V_box) time (2.66 ms across 2,759 cubes inside a 23x24x24 padded grid): shifts coordinates by (min - 1) so zero/negative coordinates map strictly inside [1..size-2] for branch-free 6-neighbor face counting, deduplicates duplicate inputs, guards sparse bounding volume in BigInt, and exposes ExteriorFlood + traceExteriorSurface + dual HiDPI Canvas visualizers (rotatable isometric painter's-order cutaway + XY slice viewer) for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against independent Set<string> 6N - 2E and bounding-box BFS oracles across official examples (10, 64, 58), hollow/breached/nested shells, and 40 seeded random 3D voxel clusters.
parts.complexity: O(N + V_box) time, O(V_box) space
learnings: Padding the 3D bounding box by 1 voxel on all 6 sides maps all lava cubes strictly inside [1..size-2], eliminating inner bounds checks during 6-neighbor face counting while guaranteeing a connected outer shell seeded at (0, 0, 0) for Part 2 exterior BFS.
Replacing a ~8,000-polygon isometric SVG with a HiDPI painter's-order Canvas renderer with interior-face occlusion culling keeps 2,759-cube playback smooth at 60 FPS with zero DOM churn.

parts.title: Boiling Boulders
parts.summary: Compute only the exterior surface area of the 3D lava droplet reachable by outside water and steam expanding orthogonally, excluding faces bordering sealed interior air pockets.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn ExteriorFlood BFS specialization reusing 2022/day18/shared VoxelDroplet, ExteriorFlood, traceExteriorSurface, and dual-canvas DropletVisualizer with zero shared edits (3.76 ms across 2,759 cubes): seeds iterative 6-connected Int32Array BFS from padded corner (0, 0, 0) to partition CELL_EXTERIOR from CELL_TRAPPED_AIR and counts lava faces adjoining exterior air; differentially verified against an independent Set<string> 6-connected BFS oracle across official example (58), 6-cube diagonal-pinch octahedron (30), hollow 3x3x3/4x4x4 shells, nested/breached 5x5x5 shells, and 5 seeded random 3D blobs.
parts.complexity: O(N + V_box) time, O(V_box) space
learnings: Pre-building ExteriorFlood and exterior-mode slice coloring in 2022/day18/shared/ delivered Part 2 with 19 lines of domain solver code and zero shared-module edits.
Testing a 6-cube diagonal-pinch octahedron (36 total -> 30 exterior) and a nested 5x5x5 shell with a floating inner cube explicitly validates 6-connectivity and inner-island face exclusion.

parts.title: Not Enough Minerals
parts.summary: Evaluate 30 robot factory blueprints over a 24-minute horizon to maximize cracked geodes per blueprint, compute each blueprint's quality level (id * maxGeodes), and sum all quality levels.
parts.algorithmSummary: Jump-to-next-robot-build Branch-and-Bound DFS with exact surplus-stock pruning and a provably admissible 3-tier decoupled relaxation upper bound in 2022/day19/shared/ (1.94 ms across all 30 blueprints): fast-forwards directly to each candidate robot's earliest affordable minute with immediate geode accounting (geodes += remAfter), enforces exact remAfter bounds (1/3/3/5) and monotonic surplus-stock bounds, captures zero-allocation optimal build plans verified by simulatePlan, and exposes multiplyMaxGeodes + FactoryVisualizer ('quality-sum' | 'geode-product') for zero-churn 32-minute Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against an independent unpruned minute-by-minute memoized brute-force DFS oracle plus official T=24 (9, 12 -> 33) and T=32 (56, 62) benchmarks.
parts.complexity: Branch-and-bound exponential worst-case; ~10^2-10^4 pruned nodes/blueprint at T=24, O(T) stack space
learnings: Macro-jumping to each robot type's earliest build minute paired with a provably admissible 3-tier decoupled relaxation upper bound (free ore, independent clay/obsidian/geode builds) solves all 30 blueprints in 1.94 ms without risking the classic inadmissible 'build geode else obsidian' bug.

Proving monotonicity of surplus stock D(k) = res + (k - 1) * bots - k * maxCost guarantees exact surplus pruning when bots < maxCost, while keeping maxGeodes and qualityLevel as dynamic getters on BlueprintResult prevents derived-state drift.

parts.title: Not Enough Minerals
parts.summary: Extend the factory horizon to 32 minutes for only the first three blueprints, maximize cracked geodes for each, and return the product of those three maxima.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn 32-minute top-3 specialization reusing 2022/day19/shared BlueprintOptimizer (jump-to-next-build branch-and-bound + 3-tier decoupled relaxation upper bound + monotonic surplus pruning), multiplyMaxGeodes, buildFactoryTrace, and FactoryVisualizer ('geode-product') with zero shared edits (2.44 ms across the first 3 blueprints at T = 32); verified by replaying every optimal 32-minute plan through simulatePlan, official example (56 * 62 = 3472), 4-blueprint slicing with a 0-geode 4th blueprint guard, 1-blueprint, and 0-geode product edge cases.
parts.complexity: Branch-and-bound exponential worst-case; ~10^3-10^4 pruned nodes/blueprint at T=32, O(T) stack space
learnings: The provably admissible 3-tier decoupled relaxation bound and exact surplus pruning scale effortlessly from 24 to 32 minutes, solving all 3 Part 2 blueprints in 2.44 ms with 23 lines of domain solver code and zero shared-module edits.
Placing a 0-geode blueprint in slot #4 of the 4-blueprint slicing test turns any accidental off-by-one slice bug into an immediate product collapse to 0.

parts.title: Grove Positioning System
parts.summary: Mix a circular list of 5,000 signed integers once in original file order (moving each entry by its own value around the remaining N - 1 elements) and sum the values at offsets +1000, +2000, and +3000 after 0.
parts.algorithmSummary: Sqrt-decomposed SqrtCircularList (blocks + Int32Array blockOf with automatic 2B block splitting and empty-block compaction) + exact BigInt Euclidean modulo (N - 1) in 2022/day20/shared/ (5.80 ms on 5,000 items): tracks entries by original identity id (handling duplicates cleanly), computes zeroId and GroveCoordinates.sum dynamically, preserves 0/+1k/+2k/+3k/active landmarks in 64-slot SVG ring sampling, and parameterizes MixConfig (rounds, decryptionKey) for zero-churn 10-round Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against an independent naive Array.splice circular oracle across official Part 1 (3) and Part 2 (1623178306) examples, duplicate-heavy lists, +/- (N - 1) wrap boundaries, N = 1..3, and 20 seeded random arrays.
parts.complexity: O(R * N * sqrt(N)) amortized time, O(N) space
learnings: Using a sqrt-decomposed block list (SqrtCircularList) keeps 5,000-element circular mixing sub-quadratic while natively returning (fromIndex, toIndex, steps) jump arcs for SVG ring visualization and staying 100% branch-testable via injectable blockSize.
Adding mandatory landmarks (0, +1k/+2k/+3k, and active toIndex) before uniform ring sampling keeps every grove coordinate and move chord visible on a 64-node SVG even for N = 5,000.

parts.title: Grove Positioning System
parts.summary: Multiply every number in the encrypted circular file by decryption key 811589153, mix the list for 10 full rounds in original file order, and sum the values at offsets +1000, +2000, and +3000 after 0.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn 10-round decryption-key specialization reusing 2022/day20/shared SqrtCircularList, exact BigInt Euclidean modulo (N - 1), solveGroveCoordinates, buildMixingTrace, and GroveMixerVisualizer with zero shared edits (21.35 ms across 50,000 relocations on 5,000 entries); differentially verified against an independent naive Array.splice 10-round oracle (comparing both exact cyclic ID permutation anchored on zeroId and grove coordinate sum) across official example (1623178306), duplicate-heavy lists, N = 1..3, and odd-low-bit BigInt values strictly above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.
parts.complexity: O(R * N * sqrt(N)) amortized time (R = 10), O(N) space
learnings: Pre-building exact BigInt Euclidean modulo (N - 1) and SqrtCircularList inside 2022/day20/shared/ solved 50,000 10-round relocations in 21.35 ms with 22 lines of Part 2 solver code and zero shared-module edits.
Comparing cyclic ID permutations anchored at zeroId against an Array.splice oracle verifies multi-round duplicate tracking independently of the 0 vs N - 1 linear wrap convention.

parts.title: Monkey Math
parts.summary: Evaluate a 2,703-monkey arithmetic expression DAG of integer literals and +, -, *, / operations to determine the exact integer yelled by root.
parts.algorithmSummary: DAG-validated bottom-up exact Rational evaluator (reusing DirectedGraph and Rational from shared/core) with polymorphic BINARY_OPERATORS (apply, applyAffine, invertLeft, invertRight) in 2022/day21/shared/ (10.16 ms across 2,703 monkeys): validates all referenced operands before constructing DirectedGraph, evaluates reachableBottomUp(root) to prevent unreachable divide-by-zero poisoning, and pre-builds exact Part 2 solveEqualityUnknown (dispatching unique-path top-down inversion vs multi-path AffineExpr elimination) + buildEqualitySolveTrace + MonkeyMathVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against an independent recursive memoized BigInt evaluator and top-down inversion + substitution oracle across official examples (152 P1, 301 P2) and seeded random trees.
parts.complexity: O(V + E) time, O(V + E) space
learnings: Evaluating only reachableBottomUp(root) prevents unreachable monkeys with division-by-zero from poisoning root while keeping Part 1 and Part 2 exact over arbitrary-precision Rational values.

Dispatching Part 2 on unknownPathCount (1n -> top-down algebraic inversion, > 1n -> AffineExpr elimination) handles both right-hand division (10 / humn = 2) and multi-path linear DAGs cleanly with zero shared-module edits.

parts.title: Monkey Math
parts.summary: Reinterpret root as an equality comparison and humn as an unknown integer variable, then solve for the exact integer humn must yell so both branches of root evaluate to the same value.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn Part 2 specialization reusing 2022/day21/shared solveEqualityUnknown (dispatching unique-path top-down exact Rational operator inversion vs multi-path AffineExpr elimination), buildEqualitySolveTrace, and MonkeyMathVisualizer with zero shared edits (9.18 ms across 2,703 monkeys); verified by substituting solved humn back into raw inputs and independently evaluating both root branches in exact Rational across the official example (301 -> 150 === 150), right-branch humn, reciprocal 10 / humn = 2 with dummy humn: 0, multi-path linear DAGs, and 20 seeded random trees spanning negative, zero, and >53-bit BigInt answers.
parts.complexity: O(V + E) time, O(V + E) space
learnings: Pre-building solveEqualityUnknown and buildEqualitySolveTrace inside 2022/day21/shared/ let Part 2 solve the 2,703-monkey equality in 9.18 ms with 21 lines of domain solver code and zero shared-module edits.

Independent raw-input substitution verification (replacing humn with the solved BigInt and evaluating both root branches in exact Rational) proves equality correctness end-to-end without sharing any inversion logic.

parts.title: Monkey Map
parts.summary: Walk a 200x150 board of open tiles, walls, and void spaces along alternating move and 90-degree turn instructions with flat row/column edge wraparound, then compute 1000*row + 4*col + facing.
parts.algorithmSummary: Polymorphic Topology strategy (FlatTorusTopology scan-back wrap + pre-built zero-churn CubeNetTopology for arbitrary 6-face cube nets via exact integer 3D orthonormal frame BFS) over an immutable Uint8Array MonkeyBoard in 2022/day22/shared/ (3.42 ms on 200x150): preserves significant leading void spaces during parsing, checks walls before committing wrapped poses (protecting pre-wrap facing on cube seams), records compressed straight-run TrailSegments + <= 240 sampled MonkeyMapTraceFrames rendered on a HiDPI canvas, and pre-verifies CubeNetTopology via exact 24-edge boundary involutions across S=4 (official Part 2 example = 5031), S=2 (011/010/110/100 net), and S=1 cube nets alongside U-shaped internal-void torus involution.
parts.complexity: O(H * W + K) time, O(H * W) space
learnings: Scanning backward by (-dr, -dc) in FlatTorusTopology instead of storing rowMin/rowMax arrays eliminates stored derived state and preserves exact topological involution even on synthetic U-shaped boards with internal void gaps.

Implementing negateVec3 as [0 - v[0], 0 - v[1], 0 - v[2]] prevents -0 values in exact 3D integer cube frames with zero branches, and folding arbitrary 6-face cube nets via coordinate-free orthonormal frames (P_B = P_tangent - (S-1)*nB + (S-1)*nA) handles every cube net shape with zero hardcoded seams.

Building an independent 3D voxel-surface sticker walker ([0..S-1]^3 with tile-level BFS rooted at row 0's leftmost playable cell) differentially verifies arbitrary cube nets without sharing any affine seam-projection math.

parts.title: Unstable Diffusion
parts.summary: Simulate 10 synchronous rounds of elf diffusion across an infinite 2D grid with rotating N/S/W/E 3-cell proposal rules and simultaneous collision cancellation, then count empty ground tiles in the tight bounding box.
parts.algorithmSummary: Dynamic padded flat Uint8Array occupancy grid + 1 KB bitmask DIR_LUT[(dirOffset << 8) | mask] + 1-based round-stamped Int32Array propTag (zero per-round array clearing, exact 2-branch collision logic backed by perpendicular-wedge 2-collider proof) in 2022/day23/shared/ (2.97 ms across 10 rounds on ~2,500 elves): stores world coordinates in elfRow/elfCol with geometric ensureMargin expansion, proves Static-Equivalence early exit (movedCount === 0 iff all elves isolated), pre-builds zero-churn Part 2 findFirstStaticRound + traceUntilStatic + HiDPI DiffusionCanvas (stable union-bounds camera), and differentially verifies round-by-round against an independent Set<string>/Map<string, number> oracle across the 5-elf (25 P1, 4 P2) and 22-elf (110 P1, 20 P2) official examples, all 4 growth borders, and seeded random grids.
parts.complexity: O(R * N + G) time, O(G + N) space
learnings: Because perpendicular proposers cover each other's 3-cell check wedges, at most two opposite elves can ever propose the same cell in a round, yielding an exact 2-branch propTag collision check with zero unreachable V8 branches.

Proving Static-Equivalence (every leading-direction extreme non-isolated elf always moves) makes early-exiting simulateRounds on movedCount === 0 exact while pre-building findFirstStaticRound and traceUntilStatic in 2022/day23/shared/ for zero-churn Part 2.

parts.title: Unstable Diffusion
parts.summary: Continue simulating synchronous elf diffusion rounds until reaching equilibrium and return the 1-based round number of the first round in which no elf moves.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn equilibrium specialization reusing 2022/day23/shared DiffusionGrid (dynamic padded flat Uint8Array + 1 KB bitmask DIR_LUT + 1-based round-stamped Int32Array propTag), findFirstStaticRound, traceUntilStatic, and DiffusionVisualizer with zero shared edits (44.72 ms across 895 rounds on ~2,500 elves); differentially verified against an independent Set<string>/Map<string, number> oracle across the official 22-elf (20) and 5-elf (4) examples, single elf (1), head-on N/S and E/W round-1 collision fixtures, and 8 seeded random clusters.

parts.title: Blizzard Basin
parts.summary: Find the fewest minutes required to cross a rectangular valley of wrapping blizzards from the top entrance to the bottom exit without occupying any blizzard cell.
parts.algorithmSummary: O(1) modular blizzard-bitmask lookup with time-layered (phase, cell) BFS over period = lcm(innerHeight, innerWidth) in 2022/day24/shared/ (22.21 ms on 25×120 inner valley, P=600): branchless modular phase lookup, exact undoAction boundary reconstruction for all grid sizes including 3×3, pre-built zero-churn Part 2 multi-leg PART2_WAYPOINTS/solveTrip/traceTrip and HiDPI BasinVisualizer, differentially verified against an independent Set-BFS oracle across the official 6×8 valley (18 / 54) and 10 seeded random valleys.
parts.complexity: O(P * H * W) time and space where P = lcm(H - 2, W - 2)
learnings: O(1) modular blizzard-bitmask lookup plus time-layered (phase, cell) BFS over P = lcm(innerH, innerW) solves a 25×120 valley in 22.21 ms with zero per-minute grid copies.
Handling entrance/exit boundary steps explicitly in undoAction guarantees exact path backtracking even on minimal 3×3 valleys where startEntryId and endEntryId coincide.
